BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.
BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.
BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.
BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.
BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.
BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.
BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.
BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.
BitField.name: TIME_STAMP

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

Enum.description: ADC analog circuits are only enabled while conversions are active. Performance is affected due to analog startup delays.
Enum.name: NOT_PRE_ENABLED

Enum.description: ADC analog circuits are pre-enabled and ready to execute conversions without startup delays (at the cost of higher DC current consumption). Note that a single power up delay (CFG[PUDLY]) is executed immediately once PWREN is set, and any detected trigger does not begin ADC operation until the power up delay time has passed. After this initial delay expires the analog remains pre-enabled and no additional delays are executed.
Enum.name: PRE_ENABLED

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: CLEAR_ON_ROLLOVER

Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Count up.
Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Count up.
Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count up.
Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Co-channel counter/timers cannot force a re-initialization of this counter/timer
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Co-channel counter/timers may force a re-initialization of this counter/timer
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Count up.
Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: TOGGLE_OFLAG_SUCCESS

Enum.name: CLEAR_ON_SECONDARY

Enum.description: Set on compare, cleared on counter rollover
Enum.name: CLEAR_ON_ROLLOVER

Enum.name: ENABLE_GATED_OUT

Enum.description: Co-channel counter/timers cannot force a re-initialization of this counter/timer
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Co-channel counter/timers may force a re-initialization of this counter/timer
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Count up.
Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: No loading action taken. Users can write new values to buffered registers (writing into outer-set of these buffered registers)
Enum.name: LDOK0

Enum.description: Outer-set values are ready to be loaded into inner-set and take effect. The loading time point depends on CTRL2[LDMOD].
Enum.name: LDOK1

Enum.description: DMA is disabled
Enum.name: DMAEN_0

Enum.description: DMA is enabled. DMA request asserts automatically when the values in the outer-set of buffered compare registers (UCOMP0/LCOMP0;UCOMP1/LCOMP1;UCOMP2/LCOMP2;UCOMP3/LCOMP3), initial registers(UINIT/LINIT) and modulus registers (UMOD/LMOD) are loaded into the inner-set of buffer and then LDOK is cleared automatically. After the completion of this DMA transfer, LDOK is set automatically, it ensures outer-set values can be loaded into inner-set which in turn triggers DMA again.
Enum.name: DMAEN_1

Enum.name: XNE1

Enum.description: INDEX pulse does not initialize the position counter
Enum.name: XIP0

Enum.description: INDEX pulse initializes the position counter
Enum.name: XIP1

Enum.description: INDEX/PRESET pulse has not occurred
Enum.name: XIRQ0

Enum.description: INDEX/PRESET pulse has occurred
Enum.name: XIRQ1

Enum.description: Standard quadrature decoder, where PHASEA and PHASEB represent a two-phase quadrature signal.
Enum.name: PH10

Enum.description: Single phase mode, bypass the quadrature decoder, refer to CTRL2[CMODE] description
Enum.name: PH11

Enum.description: Count normally and the position counter initialization uses upper/lower initialization register UINIT/LINIT
Enum.name: REV0

Enum.description: Count in the reverse direction and the position counter initialization uses upper/lower modulus register UMOD/LMOD
Enum.name: REV1

BitField.description: Software-Triggered Initialization of Position Counters UPOS and LPOS
BitField.name: SWIP

Enum.description: No action
Enum.name: SWIP0

Enum.description: Initialize position counter
Enum.name: SWIP1

BitField.description: Use Negative Edge of HOME/ENABLE Input
BitField.name: HNE

Enum.description: When CTRL[OPMODE] = 0,use HOME positive edge to trigger initialization of position counters. When CTRL[OPMODE] = 1,use ENABLE high level to enable POS/POSD/WDG/REV counters
Enum.name: HNE0

Enum.description: When CTRL[OPMODE] = 0,use HOME negative edge to trigger initialization of position counters. When CTRL[OPMODE] = 1,use ENABLE low level to enable POS/POSD/WDG/REV counters
Enum.name: HNE1

BitField.description: Enable HOME to Initialize Position Counter UPOS/LPOS
BitField.name: HIP

Enum.description: No action
Enum.name: HIP0

Enum.description: HOME signal initializes the position counter
Enum.name: HIP1

Enum.description: No transition on the HOME/ENABLE signal has occurred
Enum.name: HIRQ0

Enum.description: A transition on the HOME/ENABLE signal has occurred
Enum.name: HIRQ1

Enum.description: Decode Mode: Input nodes INDEX/PRESET and HOME/ENABLE are assigned to function of INDEX and HOME.
Enum.name: OPMODE0

Enum.description: Count Mode: Input nodes INDEX/PRESET and HOME/ENABLE are assigned to functions of PRESET and ENABLE. In this mode: (1)only when ENABLE=1, all counters (position/position difference/revolution/watchdog) can run, when ENABLE=0, all counters (position/position difference/revolution/watchdog) can't run. BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power up working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to PON_CNT_CFG value

Enum.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL2

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL3

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power up working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field
BitField.name: PON_CNT_MODE

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to PON_CNT_CFG value

Enum.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL2

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL3

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power up working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field
BitField.name: PON_CNT_MODE

Enum.description: Not use counter, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC once get Edgelock ack
Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.description: Delay after receiving Edgelock ack, delay cycle number is PON_CNT_CFG
Enum.name: VAL1

Enum.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to PON_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL2

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to PON_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL3

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power down working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field
BitField.name: POFF_CNT_MODE

Enum.description: Not use counter, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC once get Edgelock ack
Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.description: Delay after receiving Edgelock ack, delay cycle number is POFF_CNT_CFG
Enum.name: VAL1

Enum.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL2

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL3

Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.description: Delay after receiving psw ack, delay cycle number is PON_CNT_CFG

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power down working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power up working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field
BitField.name: PON_CNT_MODE

Enum.description: Not use counter, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC once get Edgelock ack
Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.description: Delay after receiving Edgelock ack, delay cycle number is PON_CNT_CFG
Enum.name: VAL1

Enum.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to PON_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL2

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to PON_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL3

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power down working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field
BitField.name: POFF_CNT_MODE

Enum.description: Not use counter, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC once get Edgelock ack
Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.description: Delay after receiving Edgelock ack, delay cycle number is POFF_CNT_CFG
Enum.name: VAL1

Enum.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL2

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL3

BitField.description: Configure the acknowledge counter for power up working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field
BitField.name: PON_CNT_MODE

Enum.description: Not use counter, raise power_on/off done to GPC once get psw ack
Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.description: Delay after receiving psw ack, delay cycle number is PON_CNT_CFG
Enum.name: VAL1

Enum.description: Ignore psw ack, raise power_on/off done to GPC when counting to PON_CNT_CFG value

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power down working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power up working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field
BitField.name: PON_CNT_MODE

Enum.description: Not use counter, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC once get Edgelock ack
Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.description: Delay after receiving Edgelock ack, delay cycle number is PON_CNT_CFG
Enum.name: VAL1

Enum.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to PON_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL2

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to PON_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL3

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power down working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field
BitField.name: POFF_CNT_MODE

Enum.description: Not use counter, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC once get Edgelock ack
Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.description: Delay after receiving Edgelock ack, delay cycle number is POFF_CNT_CFG
Enum.name: VAL1

Enum.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL2

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL3

Enum.description: Sends Edgelock handshake for power up.

Enum.name: EN

Enum.description: Sends Edgelock handshake for power down.

Enum.description: Use original signal as ack

BitField.description: Configure the acknowledge counter for power up working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field
BitField.name: PON_CNT_MODE

Enum.description: Not use counter, raise power_on/off done to GPC once get psw ack
Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.description: Delay after receiving psw ack, delay cycle number is PON_CNT_CFG
Enum.name: VAL1

Enum.description: Ignore psw ack, raise power_on/off done to GPC when counting to PON_CNT_CFG value
Enum.name: VAL2

Enum.description: Time out mode, raise power_on/off done to GPC when either psw ack received or counting to PON_CNT_CFG value

BitField.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power down working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field

Enum.name: VAL0

Enum.name: VAL3

Enum.description: No L3 header present. Indicates to the parser of not parsing the L3 header. Parsing in this case would go as far as the L2 header regardless of whether or not there is an L3 header in the frame. This option should not be used if there are any table lookup entries that contain L3/L4 key fields that could be matched against a frame.

This option should not be used if there are any table lookup entries that contain L4 key fields that could be matched against a frame.

BitField.description: Ingress Stream Forwarding Discard Reason Occurs if frame is associated with an ingress stream whose Forwarding Action (FA) is equal to discard

BitField.name: SGOEDR

BitField.name: MSDUEDR

BitField.description: Frame Modification Misconfiguration Error Discard Reason Cleared when written to 1

BitField.name: CMDR

BitField.name: ITEDR

BitField.description: Layer 2 Denial of Service Discard Reason Occurs if a packet is discarded due to L2DOS protection

BitField.description: Invalid Enqueue Port or Queue Discard Reason

BitField.description: Egress Stream Sequence Recovery Duplicate Discard Reason Occurs if packet's sequence_number is a duplicate applies for either Match or Vector Recovery Algorithm)

BitField.name: CMDR

BitField.description: Layer 2 Denial of Service Discard Reason Occurs if a packet is discarded due to L2DOS protection

Enum.description: No L3 header present. Indicates to the parser of not parsing the L3 header. Parsing in this case would go as far as the L2 header regardless of whether or not there is an L3 header in the frame. This option should not be used if there are any table lookup entries that contain L3/L4 key fields that could be matched against a frame.

Enum.description: No L4 header present. Indicates to the parser of not parsing the L4 header. Parsing in this case would go as far as the L3 header if configured to parse it (L3HFP=1) regardless of whether or not there is an L4 header in the frame. This option should not be used if there are any table lookup entries that contain L4 key fields that could be matched against a frame.
Enum.name: L4_HDR_NOT_PRESENT

Enum.description: Parse L4 header if present in the frame
Enum.name: L4_HDR_PRESENT
